raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

When `VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS=1`, upcast logits **before temperature division** in the shared unfused FSDP/VeOmni postprocessing helper. Casting only after low-precision division cannot recover the rounding already introduced.

Unset/0 preserves the existing dtype and unit-temperature no-copy path. The option keeps the lm_head matmul in its original dtype, adds no diagnostic printing, and does not affect fused loss kernels that bypass this helper. FP32 vocabulary tensors use more memory; the option is explicit and off by default.

### Duplicate-work check

Searched [FP32 logits](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+FP32+logits) and [VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS) on 2026-10-28.

- #8004 changes the lm_head projection compute precision and has different model/device constraints; this changes postprocessing only.
- #8026 adds batch-invariant FSDP execution and a sampler logprob formula using unscaled logits. This smaller option applies at the shared helper, including ordinary non-batch-invariant FSDP/VeOmni consumers and their entropy/other uses of the scaled logits. It does not claim the complete sampler formula or batch invariance from #8026.
- #8377 changes numerical stability inside torch logprob calculation; this addresses the earlier temperature-division rounding.

This draft is independent of the MiniMax model/LoRA drafts and has no pending VeOmni source dependency. Maintainer feedback on a typed configuration field versus the opt-in worker environment flag is welcome before merge.

### Test

Base: main `2ab35292039a51175a4b3d3b3b2d76e951a0d3e4`. The patch was applied to the complete current engine source file, not just the original helper fixture.

- **5 CPU tests pass** for FP16/BF16 cast order, unit temperature, unset/disabled behavior, preservation of inputs, gradients and temperature clamping.
- The same test suite fails on the unchanged helper. Test execution extracts the actual helper AST, so it does not import the full engine.
- Scoped Ruff 0.13.1 lint/format passed for both changed files. Only unused test imports and formatting were cleaned up from the reviewed draft; the runtime delta is unchanged.
- Command: `python tests/workers/engine/test_fp32_temperature_on_cpu.py -v`.
- Full resolved-checkout pre-commit, complete engine/Ray integration, native accelerator execution and peak-memory measurement have not been run for this port.

### Historical evidence

On the same archived BF16 training logits, with sampler and norm fixes already enabled, mean absolute probability difference changed from **0.006243378492 to 0.005188585780 (16.8946% lower)** when FP32 postprocessing was added.

The 2026-10-18 experiment used a historical MiniMax-M3 checkpoint with 60 text layers and **8 routed experts**, not full 128-expert M3.1-Flash. All four archived variants shared 64 responses and 54,762 valid response tokens, with image-token correction present throughout. The combined sampler + norm + postprocessing result was 0.014523769978 to 0.005188585780 (64.2752% lower). These are conditional, sequential contributions; they must not be added or attributed entirely to this PR. Sampler mode changes the probability being reported and is not an equivalent change in forward-logit error.

The archived 16-NPU GRPO diagnostic iteration completed rollout, backward and weight synchronization: 64 responses / 56,409 valid response tokens, mean probability difference 0.005803629756, gradient norm 0.054521188140, and exit 0. Its learning rate was 0, so this verifies the execution path, not learning progress. This is archived evidence, not a new hardware run of this port. The 2026-10-24 attempt failed before a complete update and contributes no new metric.

The archived launcher set `VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS=1` and `VERL_POLICY_FP32_HEAD=0`; all 16 training ranks recorded activation on BF16 logits, and the runtime source hashes matched the saved candidate. Historical CPU checks also passed for default behavior, the FP32 numerical oracle, gradients and unit temperature. Rechecking the saved helper against this PR confirms equivalent computation after excluding the one-time diagnostic print and normalizing the disabled environment default.

Historical commands were `bash real_step/run.sh` (the archived configured 16-NPU driver) and the paired postprocessing entry point `run_train_pair.sh` / `train_pair.py`. These are existing experiment artifacts, not commands rerun on the current PR checkout. The contributor asked to use their existing experiments as relevant validation; the five new CPU regressions above were run separately by the assistant.

### Usage and acceptance

Set the non-sensitive flag consistently in **all Ray worker environments** that compute policy/reference probabilities:

```text
VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS=1
```

Only the literal value 1 enables it. A launcher-shell export alone is insufficient if the worker environment does not inherit it. Check vocabulary-tensor peak memory on the intended workload. Fused loss paths need separate treatment.

### Checklist before submission / requesting merge

- [x] Human reviewed the original runtime delta on 2026-10-28.
- [x] Complete current source-file application and scoped CPU/Ruff checks passed.
- [x] Related PR scope compared and explained.
- [x] Relevant historical CPU and accelerator validation identified in the submitting user's experiment archive and checked against the runtime delta.
- [x] Current five-test regression suite and test-only import/format cleanup checked by the assistant; no claim that the human reran this new suite.
- [ ] Full repository pre-commit and engine/backend acceptance before merge.
- [ ] Maintainer CI request.

AI assistance was used for source comparison, historical evidence recomputation, tests and draft preparation. The submitting user's prior review confirmation and existing experiment evidence are recorded separately from the assistant's current regression execution. No fresh hardware acceptance or additional human execution of the new test suite is claimed.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+import ast
+import os
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+import torch
+
+SOURCE_PATH = "verl/workers/engine/fsdp/transformer_impl.py"
+ROOT = next(p for p in Path(__file__).resolve().parents if (p / SOURCE_PATH).is_file())
+TREE = ast.parse((ROOT / SOURCE_PATH).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+NODE = next(n for n in TREE.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == "_scale_logits_by_temperature")
+SCOPE = {"os": os, "torch": torch}
+exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[NODE], type_ignores=[]), SOURCE_PATH, "exec"), SCOPE)
+scale = SCOPE["_scale_logits_by_temperature"]
+
+
+class TestFP32Logits(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_default_unit_temperature_is_identity(self):
+        with patch.dict(os.environ, {}, clear=True):
+            x = torch.randn(2, 17).bfloat16()
+            self.assertIs(scale(x, 1.0, is_unit_temperature=True), x)
+
+    def test_disabled_retains_original_dtype_and_result(self):
+        x = torch.linspace(-3, 3, 34).reshape(2, 17).bfloat16()
+        t = torch.tensor([[0.7], [1.3]])
+        for flag in ("0", "false"):
+            with patch.dict(os.environ, {"VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS": flag}):
+                actual = scale(x, t, is_unit_temperature=False)
+                self.assertEqual(actual.dtype, x.dtype)
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(actual, x / t.to(x.dtype)))
+
+    def test_upcast_precedes_temperature_and_preserves_inputs(self):
+        for dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
+            with self.subTest(dtype=dtype), patch.dict(os.environ, {"VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS": "1"}):
+                x = torch.linspace(-3, 3, 34).reshape(2, 17).to(dtype)
+                t = torch.tensor([[0.7], [1.3]])
+                xb, tb = x.clone(), t.clone()
+                actual = scale(x, t, is_unit_temperature=False)
+                self.assertEqual(actual.dtype, torch.float32)
+                torch.testing.assert_close(actual, x.float() / t, rtol=0, atol=0)
+                self.assertFalse(torch.equal(actual, (x / t.to(dtype)).float()))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(x, xb))
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(t, tb))
+
+    def test_opt_in_unit_temperature(self):
+        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS": "1"}):
+            x = torch.randn(2, 17).bfloat16()
+            actual = scale(x, 1.0, is_unit_temperature=True)
+            self.assertEqual(actual.dtype, torch.float32)
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(actual, x.float()))
+            xf = x.float()
+            self.assertIs(scale(xf, 1.0, is_unit_temperature=True), xf)
+
+    def test_gradient_and_clamp(self):
+        with patch.dict(os.environ, {"VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS": "1"}):
+            x = torch.randn(2, 17).bfloat16().requires_grad_()
+            t = torch.tensor([[0.7], [1.3]])
+            scale(x, t, is_unit_temperature=False).sum().backward()
+            expected = (torch.ones(2, 17) / t).bfloat16()
+            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(x.grad, expected))
+            result = scale(torch.ones(1, 1).bfloat16(), torch.zeros(1, 1), is_unit_temperature=False)
+            self.assertTrue(torch.isfinite(result).all())
+            torch.testing.assert_close(result, torch.full((1, 1), 1e8))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

@@ -98,6 +98,12 @@ def _is_scalar_unit_temperature(temperature) -> bool:
 def _scale_logits_by_temperature(logits, temperature, *, is_unit_temperature: bool):
     """Scale logits without copying the full vocabulary tensor for temperature 1."""
 
+    # Match inference postprocessing: upcast before temperature division,
+    # while retaining the default dtype and no-copy unit-temperature path.
+    # This does not change the lm_head matmul precision.
+    if os.environ.get("VERL_POLICY_FP32_LOGITS", "0") == "1":
+        logits = logits.float()
+
     if is_unit_temperature:
         return logits
     return logits / temperature.clamp(min=1e-8).to(logits.dtype)
